title: Satisfaction of the encoded clause
statement: Let $V$ be a variable type, let $\alpha:V\to\mathrm{Prop}$ be an assignment, let $i$ be a clause index, and let $C$ be a finite clause over $V$. Suppose some literal of $C$ is true under $\alpha$. Extend $\alpha$ to the original and auxiliary variables by giving each original variable its value under $\alpha$, assigning the auxiliary variable with indices $(r,j)$ the truth value that the first $j+2$ literals of $C$ are all false when $r=i$, and assigning it false when $r\ne i$. Then every 3-clause in the encoding of $C$ at index $i$ is satisfied by this extended assignment.
hypotheses_covered: At least one literal of $C$ is true under $\alpha$
replaced:
Let $\alpha$ be a truth assignment on a variable set $V$, and let $C$ be a clause over
$V$ — a finite list of literals read as their disjunction — carrying the index $i$.
Assume $\alpha$ satisfies $C$, meaning at least one literal of $C$ is true under
$\alpha$. Extend $\alpha$ to an assignment $\alpha_3$ on the enlarged variable set
consisting of the original variables of $V$ together with the auxiliary chain variables
$y_{i,j}$: leave each original variable at its value under $\alpha$, and set $y_{i,j}$
to true exactly when the first $j+2$ literals of $C$ are all false under $\alpha$. Then
every $3$-clause in the list obtained by encoding $C$ at index $i$ as $3$-clauses is
satisfied by $\alpha_3$.
